How each POSIXct-valued op gets its zone (F32)

Source: R/ir.R
ir_tz_rules.Rd

Verified against dplyr 1.2 / vctrs 0.7 on plain tibbles, for local, absent, UTC and New York operands:

Usage

ir_tz_rules

Format

A named list of op names per rule

Details

  • x: the result is x itself, a slice of it, or other values cast to x's type (vec_cast(y, x)), so it has x's zone (absent becomes ""): na_if(), replace_when() (also replace_values()), lag()/ lead() (with default = ), first()/last()/nth(), min()/ max(), mean()/median() (F41), and cuplyr's roll_min()/roll_max().

  • common: vctrs' common type of the value operands in order (tz_fold()), then absent becomes "": if_else() (true, false, missing), case_when() (values in order, then .default), coalesce().

  • as_posixct: a POSIXct keeps its zone as is, a Date becomes UTC midnight (R's as.POSIXct.Date).

  • shift (F46): ts_add_us/ts_sub_us keep x's zone attribute as is (an absent one stays absent).

  • round_date (F46): round_date() of a local or absent zone returns the session zone's name; floor_date()/ceiling_date() (in x) keep "".

Not listed, so CPU: unary -, abs(), cummax()/cummin() (R's Math.POSIXt rejects them, so dplyr errors). A bare t +/- n never reaches here: its type check sends it to the CPU (infer_mutate_output_type()); only the rounding calls rewrite it (ir_posixct_shift()).
